key_insight: A self-balancing sequential sampler adaptively biases choices so the empirical distribution reaches a target law at the optimal O(n^-1) rate while remaining difficult to predict.
engineering_relevance: This can improve audit schedules, representative sampling, and treatment assignment by reducing repeated selections and long gaps without sacrificing unpredictability.
method: Adaptive Markovian sampling with biasing rules that steer counts toward the target distribution
Entropy-regularized optimization to trade off fast convergence against sample unpredictability
Stochastic mirror-descent view plus a weak-bias diffusion limit leading to an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck approximation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and explicit convergence results, including a fastest-possible O(n^-1) rate, uniqueness under an entropy-regularized objective, and a diffusive-limit characterization.
watch_item: Performance depends on the chosen biasing parameters, so overly aggressive settings may reduce unpredictability or make implementation tuning nontrivial.
paper_title: Self-Balancing Sequential Sampling: Fast Convergence with Controlled Predictability
